title: Who's your favorite youtuber for developing/designing games with AI?
author: SquirrelTomahawk
selftext: Looking for guidance from good youtube channels. Thank you

comments.author: BenTheSodaman
comments.body:
There's no way around me not sounding like I'm shilling at this point. 

[https://www.youtube.com/@1dudedevteam/videos](https://www.youtube.com/@1dudedevteam/videos) /

 [https://www.youtube.com/@WerewolvenGames/](https://www.youtube.com/@WerewolvenGames/)  

While he will reference his forge tools, you don't necessarily have to use that site if you already have something that does some of the features, willing to put in the manual elbow grease, or have a load of tokens to blow to vibe a tool that does one or more of the features offered on the forge tool.

e.g., the Mac' Preview has a magic wand that serve to remove backgrounds, but far more manual if you have multiple frames to work through and will ultimately take longer than a tool with finer control over background removal and dealing with the glowing edges that AI generated images typically have. (Though GPT Image 2 can generate a PNG with transparency, but the technique can backfire when you're trying to extract frames from a video to create an animation.)

The concepts and techniques that have been helpful to me and/or get me stoked to even explore this avenue of development. But as with anything, the building blocks are presented and it'll be very much up you to interpret it correctly and refine it to a level that works for you and your project.

replies.author: Nez_Coupe
replies.body:
I say this a lot just cause I think people overestimate the difficulty. You mentioned removing backgrounds - this is a trivial Python script if you have a solid background (or at least close to the same hue/brightness) Codex or even a crappy agent / model could throw together a script in a few minutes using Python to murder millions of pixels quickly. 

Same with a lot of static tools. You can recreate 75% of the basic tools you need for editing for a $20 sub to OpenAI, honestly. You don’t need extra effort you can use medium for these tasks. 

Now there are the other 25% of tools that this will not work for complex animation or 3D. 

I built my own editing studio that has a ton of features on the cheap OAI plan. I’m just very particular about tools.

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/perslfxtxz2h1.png?width=3324&format=png&auto=webp&s=c79759591fc4838af9a6ae2d04a58d455fea45bc

This is the outcome of what you proposed on a test image. Created a tool in Codex that relies on Python script that removes the background by image or a batch of images. 2 minute prompt and tool it made without further refinements.

The character is glowing purple. For a folder worth of them, that is a lot of clean. Maybe that's acceptable to you. It's not to me.

When the background was light green, his hair, coat, and gun took a hit and he's still glowing green.

When the background was black, his pants, sleeves, and shoes took a hit.

When the background was white, he's glowing white.

Where it sounds like you're misunderstanding the issue that others have been having and downplaying it. And more work would need to go into a background removal tool than the advice you've given so far.

replies.author: Nez_Coupe
replies.body: That’s not done correctly. I’m not misunderstanding anything. You can remove the aliasing leftover, it’s you that are misunderstanding how to implement.

replies.body: For test scenarios it is ok BUT when it comes to transparency it became a disaster as you converting RGB to RGBA and my current approach is to create black background and white background versions of the same image to get true RGBA.
